name: How much contingency should I keep for a bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: How much extra money should I set aside for unexpected problems during a bathroom renovation?
mainEntity.text: How much extra money should I set aside for unexpected problems during a bathroom renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency reserve is essential because bathrooms often hide problems that are only visible after demolition starts. A reasonable starting point is 10% to 20% of the total budget, with a higher buffer for older homes or projects that involve plumbing moves and structural work. That reserve helps cover hidden water damage, rotted framing, code-related upgrades, and material substitutions if something is backordered. The goal is not to spend the contingency, but to avoid being forced into low-quality compromises when unexpected issues appear. Ask the contractor which problems are most likely in your type of home so you can size the reserve realistically. In Los Angeles-area remodels, this planning step can prevent major stress later in the job.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency for a bathroom remodel is at least 10% to 20% of the project budget, and older homes may need more. Hidden water damage, code upgrades, subfloor repairs, and material changes are the most common reasons costs rise.
